correctness.rationale: The identities A(n)=s_2(n) and B(n)=2s_2(n)-s_2(3n) follow exactly from Legendre. Since 3n is divisible by 3 but is not a power of 2, s_2(3n)>=2, hence 0<=B<=2k-2. Kummer count of carries in n+2n shows the first carry forces a second at the next bit, excluding B=1. For b=0 use z_k=(4^k-1)/3; for b=2j-2 use e_j=(2^(2j-1)+1)/3; for b=2j-3 use o_j=(2^(2j-2)+5)/3. Each has the asserted digit weight and valuation. Map P(n)=4n+1 increases A by one while fixing B, so every b=0 or b=2..2k-2 appears for all appropriate k; n->2^h*n gives infinitely many witnesses. Independent all-pair constructive check for k=1..20 tested 381 pairs and a separate direct scan n=1..9999 found no excluded value. Finite evidence is corroborative; proof covers every n and k.

value.rationale: An exact attainable-support theorem for two natural 2-adic binomial valuations is a motivated fine-scale classification; its globally forbidden value 1, sharp upper endpoint 2k-2, and explicit infinite witnesses are not obtained from marginal divisibility results or finite scans. It can be used to distinguish feasible simultaneous divisibility profiles, though it claims no asymptotic frequencies.
